steps.title: Understand place value
steps.content: A number is built from digits and place values. In 4,582, the 4 represents four thousands, the 5 five hundreds, the 8 eight tens and the 2 two ones.

steps.title: Classify a number
steps.prompt: Which of these is a prime number?
steps.explanation: 29 has exactly two positive factors: 1 and 29. The other numbers have additional factors.

steps.title: Use divisibility rules
steps.content: A number is divisible by 2 if its last digit is even; by 3 if its digit sum is divisible by 3; by 5 if it ends in 0 or 5; and by 9 if its digit sum is divisible by 9.
steps.example: 729 has digit sum 18, so it is divisible by 9 and by 3.
steps.tip: For large numbers, use divisibility rules before attempting long division.

steps.title: Find the remainder
steps.prompt: What is the remainder when 47 is divided by 5?

steps.title: Estimate multiples
steps.content: For the smallest multiple of k greater than or equal to n, find the first integer m with k×m ≥ n. This is useful in remainder, scheduling and divisibility questions.
steps.example: The smallest three-digit multiple of 7 is 7×15 = 105.

questions.prompt: How many positive factors does 12 have?
questions.explanation: The factors are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 12: six factors.

questions.prompt: What is the smallest three-digit multiple of 7?
questions.explanation: 7×14 = 98 is two-digit; 7×15 = 105 is the first three-digit multiple.

questions.prompt: Which of these is an even prime number?
questions.explanation: 2 is the only even prime; every other even integer has factor 2 and itself.

questions.prompt: What is the remainder when 83 is divided by 10?
